title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
summary: Girl with a Pearl Earring is an oil painting by Dutch Golden Age painter Johannes Vermeer, dated c. 1665. Going by various names over the centuries, it acquired its present title towards the end of the 20th century. The work has been in the collection of the Mauritshuis in The Hague since 1902 and has been the subject of various literary and cinematic treatments.

sections.name: her face
sections.description: The subject's enigmatic gaze and slightly parted lips create a sense of intimacy and mystery. Her pale skin and subtle features are softly illuminated against the dark background.

sections.name: the pearl earring
sections.description: The focal point of the piece, this large pearl earring is rendered with just a few highlights. It symbolizes wealth and adds a brilliant touch of light to the shadowed side of her face.

sections.name: the turban
sections.description: The exotic blue turban is painted using expensive ultramarine pigment, indicating her unique attire. Its folds and wrap around her head give the composition a sense of volume.

sections.name: her jacket
sections.description: Her simple brownish-yellow garment has a modest white collar, providing a grounded contrast to the elaborate headgear. The textures of the fabric are captured through soft brushwork.

museum_facts: The Mauritshuis dates the painting to around 1665 and says it is on view in Room 15.
It is not a portrait of a known person but a “tronie,” a study of an imaginary figure in exotic dress.
Vermeer used soft transitions to model the girl’s face, while small dabs of paint suggest reflected light on her clothing.
The oversized pearl is probably an imitation: Vermeer suggested it with just two brushstrokes, and painted no silver hook.

guide_notes.her face: Her face is the oval outline filling the board, with two short lines for her eyes, a small bump in the middle for her nose, and a longer line near the bottom for her mouth. A 2018 to 2020 study of the painting found tiny eyelashes around both eyes, too small to see without scanning.
guide_notes.the pearl earring: The pearl is a round oval outline, widest in the middle, with one raised ball near the upper left for its shine. Vermeer painted no hook joining it to her ear, only a few highlights, and in the 1994 restoration a second small highlight turned out to be a loose flake of paint and was removed.
guide_notes.the turban: The turban fills the board: a rounded outline that peaks at the top right, with a straight line across the fourth row where the blue band meets the yellow cloth piled above it, and the right edge running all the way down to the bottom where that cloth hangs. Its blue is natural ultramarine, ground from lapis lazuli brought from Afghanistan, one of the most expensive pigments of its time.
guide_notes.her jacket: The jacket starts narrow under her chin and spreads into a wide outline down to the bottom of the board, with one line down the middle for a fold. Vermeer painted it before the white collar, the turban and the pearl, which came last.
